name: Lug wrench
description: An L-shaped steel bar with a hex socket on its short leg for wheel nuts and a flattened tip for prying off hub caps. Heavy enough to swing.
notes: An 18 mm bar bent to a 0.40 m lever and a 0.12 m leg with a 19 mm socket, lying flat. The L shape boxes far more air than its bar. wrenching 3, the lug and large-wrench grade, covers taking wheels off vehicles. It would also make a blunt melee weapon, which needs a weapon block once tuned.

name: Makeshift hammer
description: A lump of scrap steel wired across the end of a rough wooden stick. It drives nails, badly.
notes: A 0.30 m sapling haft with a 100 mm steel offcut lashed across its end with galvanised wire. The head stands across the haft, leaving air in the box. Hammering 1 sits under the proper hammer's 2. Player-made, so it rarely spawns.

name: Leather hose
description: A length of stitched leather tube, coiled up. It holds liquid well enough to siphon fuel from a tank, though it kinks and stiffens.
notes: About 1.5 m of 18 mm hose coiled flat in three loops with a hard leather collar at each end. The open coil is mostly air. siphoning is the quality name for drawing liquid out of a tank; a rubber hose should score higher.

name: Makeshift vacuum former
description: A plywood box with a pegboard top, a hinged frame that clamps a plastic sheet above it and a hand pump on a hose. Heat the sheet, drop the frame and pump, and the plastic pulls tight over whatever sits on the board.
notes: A 300 by 240 mm box 70 mm tall with its clamp frame propped open and a rubber pump bulb on a hose at the side. The open frame and pump stand off the box. vacuum_forming is a new quality name for shaping plastic sheet into moulds.

name: Makeshift welding blanket
description: A heavy mat stitched together from oven insulation under a tough woven cover, folded into a thick square. It catches welding sparks and keeps heat in a weld while it cools.
notes: Folded to 450 by 350 mm and 70 mm thick, its quilting drawn as thin sunken lines in cloth-turnout close to the cover colour and a jute tie, so it reads as a quilted mat rather than a slatted lid. aramid-gold stands in for the cover. extinguishing 1 covers shielding surfaces from sparks and slow-cooling a weld.

name: Needle file set
description: Five slim steel files with different cuts, held in a vinyl wallet by an elastic band. For shaping small metal parts and taking off burrs.
notes: Five 140 mm needle files with red handles in a 150 by 80 mm wallet. filing is a new quality name; sharpening stands in for grinding.

name: Bronze needle file set
description: Five slim cast bronze files in a vinyl wallet. Softer than steel files, but they still shape wood, bone and soft metal.
notes: The steel set's model with the files in bronze. Made by the player, so it rarely spawns; filing 1 is a guess for the softer metal.

name: Concrete float
description: A flat iron blade with a wooden grip on a bent strap, for smoothing wet concrete, mortar and plaster.
notes: A 150 by 75 mm iron blade with a strap handle and an oak grip. filing 2 covers finishing concrete and plaster.

name: Field repair kit
description: A canvas roll holding a folding wood saw, a craft knife and a soft cleaning cloth. With tape it patches up gear in the field.
notes: A 460 by 140 mm canvas roll laid open with its saw, knife and cloth. repairing 1 is its main job; the other qualities map to cutting and sawing; butchering is set low because it is a craft knife. Repairing items with tape needs a repair field, which Deadvox tools do not have yet.

name: Multitool
description: A pair of folding pliers whose handles hide a knife blade, a small saw, a file and screwdriver bits.
notes: Shown opened out to 135 mm with its jaws forward and the tucked tools along the handles. The camping multitool rides on this model. Its saw blades map to sawing and metal_cutting, its screwdriver to screwing.

name: Bronze nail puller
description: A cast bronze bar with a curled claw at one end and a flat split claw at the other, for working nails out of boards.
notes: A 250 mm bar of 16 mm square stock with a curled claw, a striking boss behind it and a flat claw. Made by the player, so it rarely spawns.

name: Oxy-acetylene torch
description: A brass torch handle with oxygen and gas valves and a cutting head. Hooked to the right gas cylinders, it cuts through steel bars and welds metal.
notes: A 250 mm brass handle with red and blue valve knobs, a cutting attachment with its oxygen lever and copper nozzle, and two short hose tails, 0.56 m in all. The carry tote is left out. Running it needs a gas cylinder feed, which Deadvox tools have no field for; the blowtorch's canister fuel is the nearest existing shape.

name: Wall brush
description: A wide flat brush with a wooden handle, for painting walls and fences.
notes: A 100 mm brush 210 mm long: beavertail birch handle, galvanised ferrule and a block of dark bristle. painting is a new quality name.

name: Pickaxe
description: A long hardwood handle with a curved steel head, pointed on one side and chiselled on the other. It breaks rock and hard ground, and anyone strong enough can swing it at something else.
notes: A 0.85 m haft and a 0.6 m curved head lying flat. The head stands across the haft, so its bounding box is mostly air. Qualities are new names. It needs a heavy weapon block once melee is tuned.

name: Pin reamer
description: A slim tapered steel reamer with fluted edges and a knurled grip, turned by hand to widen a hole or clean its burrs.
notes: A plain 45 mm mid-grey steel handle with faint galvanised knurl rings and an 85 mm fluted taper from 8 to 3 mm. reaming is a new quality name.

name: Pliers
description: A pair of slip-joint pliers with ridged jaws and red dipped grips. Fine for loosening a stuck nut or holding something hot.
notes: The pliers family's groove kind at 170 mm, standing in for a slip joint. Locking pliers ride on this model; their lever and screw would want their own model. gripping is a new quality name.
